problem_statement.title: Multi-version bootstrap silently drops versions with no sdist
problem_statement.body:
In multi-version bootstrap mode, versions that match the specifier but have no sdist are silently filtered out during candidate resolution. No warning is logged, no entry is added to partial-failures.json, and no record exists that the version was ever considered.

## Reproduction

Package `drr` has versions 1.0.2 through 1.0.5 on PyPI. Version 1.0.4 has only a wheel (no sdist).

```
$ fromager list-versions "drr>=1.0.2" --distribution-type both
Found 4 version(s)
1.0.2
1.0.3
1.0.4
1.0.5

$ fromager list-versions "drr>=1.0.2" --distribution-type sdist
Found 3 version(s)
1.0.2
1.0.3
1.0.5
```

When bootstrapping with `--multi-version` and `drr>=1.0.2`, only 1.0.2, 1.0.3, and 1.0.5 are processed. 1.0.4 is never mentioned in logs or in partial-failures.json.

## Root cause

`PyPIProvider.validate_candidate()` in `resolver.py` ([lines 945-957](https://github.com/python-wheel-build/fromager/blob/main/src/fromager/resolver.py#L945-L957)) silently rejects candidates that don't match the desired distribution type. The debug log is gated behind `DEBUG_RESOLVER`, which is off by default.

## Expected behavior

In multi-version mode, when a version matching the specifier is dropped because it lacks an sdist, Fromager should either:
1. Log a warning (e.g., "drr==1.0.4: skipped, no sdist available on PyPI")
2. Record it in partial-failures.json with a clear reason
3. Ideally, both.

This matters for downstream observability -- operators need to know when a version exists but was not built, and why.

## Contrast with pinned versions

When pinned (`drr==1.0.4`), Fromager correctly errors out: "found no match for drr==1.0.4... searching for sdists." The gap is only in multi-version mode where other versions satisfy the requirement and the missing one is silently skipped.

problem_statement.title: Preserve order of recording extractor custom properties in `add_electrodes()`
problem_statement.body:
I noticed the order of properties that are being added to the `Electrodes` table is not in the same order as in the recording_extractor._properties, for instance:

```python
recording_extractor._properties

[...., 'electrode_type', 'chamber_type', 'chamber_x', 'chamber_y', 'chamber_z', 'acx_x', 'acx_y', 'acx_z']
```
The order of properties to add to the Electrodes table is changed at this line:
https://github.com/catalystneuro/neuroconv/blob/fa6edd532f6bb6ead42ae40aa9029c7c78eead5f/src/neuroconv/tools/spikeinterface/spikeinterface.py#L322
which does not preserve the order of the elements:

```python
['electrode_type', 'acx_x', 'chamber_type', 'chamber_z', 'channel_ids', 'acx_z', 'chamber_x', 'acx_y', 'chamber_y', 'offset_to_uV', 'gain_to_uV']
```

I think we should preserve the order of properties to be the same the `recording_extractor._properties`.

Opened https://github.com/catalystneuro/neuroconv/pull/793 as draft to discuss

problem_statement.body:
As part of the [initiative](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/issues/4805) to stabilize the Prometheus Exporter spec, the Python SDK's Prometheus Exporter should introduce support for [Default Aggregation](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/main/specification/metrics/sdk_exporters/prometheus.md#default-aggregation) configuration to align with the spec.

The current implementation status is documented in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/issues/4986#issuecomment-4214660688.

**Describe the bug**
When parsing a segment of SQL, although the field-level relationships exist, the source table information is lost.
 existing table prefixes have also been replaced with "default.".

**SQL**
Paste the SQL text here. For example:
```sql=
insert into foo.tb1  select f1,f2,(select f3 from  bar.tb1) b3 from  foo.tb2
```


For example:
```pycharm  run 

MetaData = {"bar.tb1": ["f1", "f2", "f3"]}

provider = DummyMetaDataProvider(MetaData)

LineageRunner = sqllineage.runner.LineageRunner(sql, metadata_provider=provider, verbose=True)

LineageRunner.print_column_lineage()
print("=======source_tables:")
print(LineageRunner.source_tables)
```

result:
```
foo.tb1.b3 <- <default>.tb1.f3
foo.tb1.f1 <- foo.tb2.f1
foo.tb1.f2 <- foo.tb2.f2
=======source_tables:
[Table: foo.tb2]
```


**Expected behavior**
I hope to correctly display the prefix **bar. for  tb1.f3**    and **bar.tb1 in source_tables**

**Python version (available via `python --version`)**
 - 3.8.17


**SQLLineage version (available via `sqllineage --version`):**
 - 1.5.3

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.

problem_statement.title: v0.3 gRPC compat drops task status timestamp and three other fields
problem_statement.body:
## What happens

Over the v0.3 gRPC compat endpoint, task statuses have no `timestamp`. The v0.3 JSON-RPC and REST compat endpoints include it.

Round trip through `compat/v0_3/proto_utils.py`:

```
timestamp after gRPC round trip: None      (sent 2026-03-15T10:30:00Z)
icon_url: None                              (sent http://x/icon.png)
skill security: None                        (sent [{'oauth': ['read']}])
```

`OAuth2SecurityScheme.oauth2_metadata_url` is dropped the same way.

## Why

`proto_utils.py` doesn't map these four fields in either direction. `conversions.py`, used by the JSON-RPC and REST compat paths, maps all four.

## Version

main @ f3ac824

problem_statement.title: SFTTrainer does not append EOS when dataset_text_field is not "text"
problem_statement.body:
### Reproduction

`SFTTrainer._prepare_dataset` appends the EOS token to standard (non-conversational) language-modeling examples, but the `add_eos` step only looks for a column literally named `"text"`, while the tokenization step reads `example[args.dataset_text_field]`. With a custom `dataset_text_field`, no EOS is ever appended, silently: no error, no warning, the sequences just never end with `eos_token_id`.

```python
import tempfile

from datasets import load_dataset
from trl import SFTConfig, SFTTrainer

MODEL = "trl-internal-testing/tiny-Qwen2ForCausalLM-2.5"
dataset = load_dataset("trl-internal-testing/zen", "standard_language_modeling", split="train")

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    for field in ["text", "content"]:
        ds = dataset if field == "text" else dataset.rename_column("text", field)
        args = SFTConfig(output_dir=tmp, dataset_text_field=field, use_cpu=True, report_to="none")
        trainer = SFTTrainer(model=MODEL, args=args, train_dataset=ds)
        eos_id = trainer.processing_class.eos_token_id
        n_with_eos = sum(example["input_ids"][-1] == eos_id for example in trainer.train_dataset)
        print(f"dataset_text_field={field!r}: {n_with_eos}/{len(trainer.train_dataset)} examples end with EOS ({eos_id})")
        print("  example[0] input_ids:", trainer.train_dataset[0]["input_ids"])
```

outputs:

```
dataset_text_field='text': 17/17 examples end with EOS (151645)
  example[0] input_ids: [46518, 374, 2664, 1091, 27261, 13, 151645]
dataset_text_field='content': 0/17 examples end with EOS (151645)
  example[0] input_ids: [46518, 374, 2664, 1091, 27261, 13]
```

Expected: both runs end every example with `151645` (`<|im_end|>`), since `dataset_text_field` is documented as "Name of the column that contains text data in the dataset" and the rest of the pipeline already honours it.

Cause (`trl/trainer/sft_trainer.py`, `_prepare_dataset`, unchanged since #3328):

```python
def add_eos(example, eos_token):
    if "text" in example and not example["text"].endswith(eos_token):  # language modeling case
        example["text"] = example["text"] + eos_token
    elif "completion" in example and not example["completion"].endswith(eos_token):
        example["completion"] = example["completion"] + eos_token
    return example
```

whereas `tokenize_fn` uses `example[dataset_text_field]`. The other trainers' `add_eos` copies (DPO/KTO/Reward) only deal with `chosen`/`rejected`/`completion`, so this is SFT-only.

Fix: pass `args.dataset_text_field` into `add_eos` and use it instead of the literal `"text"`. I have a 3-line patch plus a parametrized regression test (`["text", "content"]`) ready and can open a PR.

+    When ``document_only`` is true, only PDF document blocks are removed

+    stripping applies only to blocks nested inside tool results, so

-    should_strip = _is_audio_block if audio_only else _is_media_block

@@ -195,7 +239,7 @@ def _strip_media_blocks_in_place(

problem_statement.title: [Bug] Tool-returned image/PDF binary sent as bare base64 ("type":"data") triggers 400 "file must have a file_id or file_data"
problem_statement.body:
> This issue was drafted with the assistance of an AI agent (**deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp**).
> 本 issue 由 AI agent（**deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp**）代笔。

## Summary

When an **agent tool returns an image or PDF binary** (e.g. `send_file_to_user`, `view_image`, or any tool whose result carries base64 media), QwenPaw serializes it into the model request as a bare `{"type": "data", "data": "<base64>"}` content part — **without a `data:<mime>;base64,` URI prefix**. Providers that lint content parts (e.g. DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible endpoint) reject it with:

```
openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'file must have a file_id or file_data', ...}}
```

The user-visible error is a generic `claw internal error` / `internal error`, masking the real cause.

## Environment

- **QwenPaw**: 2.2.0 (python3.13, Debian)
- **Provider**: DeepSeek OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint, vision model
- **Channel**: console / `default` agent
- **Trigger**: agent invokes a tool that returns an image/PDF; the tool result binary is injected into the message history

## Repro

1. Configure a DeepSeek vision model as the active model.
2. Send the agent a request that causes it to use a tool whose result contains an image or PDF (e.g. `send_file_to_user` a PDF, `view_image` a local file, or any tool returning base64 media).
3. The agent tries to call the model again with the tool result in context.

**Actual**: `400 BadRequestError: file must have a file_id or file_data`.

## Diagnosis

The error occurs at `messages[43]`. Dumping the failing request shows the offending content part(s):

```json
{
  "type": "data",
  "data": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAA...",   // PNG magic bytes, bare base64
  ...
}
```

A failing request contains **10** such `{"type": "data", "data": "<base64>"}` parts. Critically:

- No `data:` MIME prefix (it is *not* `data:image/png;base64,...`).
- No `image_url` wrapper.
- No `media_type` field.

The same builder correctly emits `data:image/png;base64,` in the image-probe path (`openai_provider.py` `_probe_image_support`), so this is a **missed path in tool-result / message serialization**, not a general inability to handle media.

## Root-cause location

- `qwenpaw/_compat/message.py` — for `user` messages the allowed content-part types include `{"text", "data"}`, and tool-returned binary is carried as a `{type: "data", data: <b64>}` block.
- The provider / chat-model serialization layer forwards that block to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint **as-is** instead of converting it to the expected `{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:<mime>;base64,<data>"}}`.

## Suggested fix

In the message serialization path, when emitting an OpenAI-compatible request:

- If a content part is `{type: "data", data: <b64>}` with a known `media_type`, wrap it as `data:image/png;base64,...` / `data:application/pdf;base64,...` data URL and emit `{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": <data-url>}}`.
- If `media_type` is unknown, either infer it from the magic bytes or degrade gracefully (skip the part / replace with a short text stub) rather than sending an invalid part.

## Notes / related

- Clearing historical bad content parts is only a workaround: fresh tool-returned media re-triggers the error every time. This is a serialization bug, not a stale-data problem.
- Possibly related: #7516, #7370 (base64 data URIs on WeCom), #7051 (image attachments lost on session reload).

---

## 中文版

> 本 issue 由 AI agent（**deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp**）代笔起草。经用户（仓库维护者/使用者）确认后发布，用于向 QwenPaw 项目反馈缺陷。

### 概述

当 **agent 工具返回图片或 PDF 二进制**（例如 `send_file_to_user`、`view_image`，或任何结果携带 base64 媒体的工具）时，QwenPaw 在发给模型的请求里会把它序列化成裸的 `{"type": "data", "data": "<base64>"}` content part —— **缺少 `data:<mime>;base64,` 前缀**。会对 content part 做校验的 provider（例如 DeepSeek 的 OpenAI 兼容端点）会拒绝它并报错：

```
openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'file must have a file_id or file_data', ...}}
```

用户实际看到的是通用的 `claw internal error` / `internal error`，掩盖了真实原因。

### 环境

- **QwenPaw**：2.2.0（python3.13，Debian）
- **Provider**：DeepSeek OpenAI 兼容 chat completions 端点，视觉模型
- **通道**：console / `default` agent
- **触发条件**：agent 调用一个返回图片/PDF 的工具；工具结果二进制被注入消息历史

### 复现

1. 将 DeepSeek 视觉模型配置为 active model。
2. 向 agent 发送一个会触发它使用某工具（结果含图片/PDF，例如 `send_file_to_user` 发 PDF、`view_image` 读本地文件，或任何返回 base64 媒体的工具）的请求。
3. 下一次带着工具结果调用模型。

**实际结果**：`400 BadRequestError: file must have a file_id or file_data`。

### 诊断

错误发生在 `messages[43]`。导出失败的请求可见问题 content part：

```json
{
  "type": "data",
  "data": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAA...",   // PNG 魔数，裸 base64
  ...
}
```

一个失败请求里包含 **10** 个这样的 `{"type":"data","data":"<base64>"}` part。关键点：

- 没有 `data:` MIME 前缀（它**不是** `data:image/png;base64,...`）。
- 没有 `image_url` 包裹。
- 没有 `media_type` 字段。

同一构建逻辑在 image-probe 路径（`openai_provider.py` `_probe_image_support`）里会正确生成 `data:image/png;base64,`，所以这是**工具结果/消息序列化路径上的遗漏**，而不是不能处理媒体。

### 根因定位

- `qwenpaw/_compat/message.py` —— 对 `user` 消息，允许的 content part 类型包含 `{"text","data"}`，工具返回二进制被作为 `{type:"data", data:<b64>}` block 携带。
- provider / chat-model 序列化层把该 block **原样**转发给 OpenAI 兼容端点，而没有转换成期望的 `{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"data:<mime>;base64,<data>"}}`。

### 建议修复

在消息序列化路径、发包给 OpenAI 兼容请求时：

- 如果 content part 是 `{type:"data", data:<b64>}` 且已知 `media_type`，则包成 `data:image/png;base64,...` / `data:application/pdf;base64,...` data URL，并输出 `{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":<data-url>}}`。
- 如果 `media_type` 未知，则从 magic bytes 推断，或优雅降级（跳过该 part / 用简短文本占位），而不是发送一个无效 part。

### 备注 / 相关

- 只清历史坏 content part 只是权宜之计：每次新增工具返回媒体都会重新触发。这是序列化 bug，不是旧数据问题。
- 可能相关：#7516、#7370（WeCom 的 base64 data URI）、#7051（session 重载时图片附件丢失）。

problem_statement.title: Nested Jinja context not working when defined in pyproject.toml (since 3.2.0 only)
problem_statement.body:
### Search before asking

- [X] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

Nested Python dictionaries used as Jinja context variables are no longer handled correctly in `sqlfluff` 3.2.0 and up, when defined in `pyproject.toml` and not `.sqlfluff`.

### Expected Behaviour

Sample SQL:
```sql
select
    {% for metric in bundle.selected_metrics -%}
        coalesce({{ metric.definition }}, 0)::float as {{ metric.name }},
    {% endfor -%}
    '123' as bar
from data;
```

Sample pyproject.toml:

```toml 
[tool.sqlfluff.templater.jinja.context]
bundle  = {safe_name = 'test_metric', base_sql = 'select 1', join_key = 'user_id', selected_metrics = [{name = 'logged_days', definition='COUNT(*)'}]}

[tool.sqlfluff.core]
templater = "jinja"
dialect = "snowflake"
```

sample `.sqlfluff`:
```
[sqlfluff]
templater = jinja
dialect=snowflake

[sqlfluff:templater:jinja:context]
bundle = {'safe_name': 'test_metric', 'base_sql': 'select 1', 'join_key': 'user_id', 'selected_metrics' : [{'name':'logged_days', 'definition':'COUNT(*)'}]}
```

Expected behavior: linting passes successfully, such as when using `.sqlfluff`

```
uvx sqlfluff lint test.sql --config .sqlfluff --ignore-local-config --- passes
```




### Observed Behaviour

The same configuration fails when using pyproject.toml

```
uvx sqlfluff lint test.sql --config pyproject.toml --ignore-local-config
== [test.sql] FAIL
L:   2 | P:   1 | LT02 | Line should not be indented. [layout.indent]
L:   2 | P:  49 | LT02 | Expected indent of 4 spaces. [layout.indent]
L:   3 | P:  17 |  PRS | Line 2, Position 13: Found unparsable section: "(,
                       | 0)::float as ,\n    '123' as bar"
WARNING: Parsing errors found and dialect is set to 'snowflake'. Have you configured your dialect correctly?
All Finished 📜 🎉!

```

However, it works with sqlfluff 3.1.1:

```
uvx sqlfluff@3.1.1 lint test.sql --config pyproject.toml --ignore-local-config
All Finished 📜 🎉!
```



### How to reproduce

See above.

### Dialect

snowflake (likely dialect independent)

### Version

Tested with both 3.3.0 and 3.2.0/3.2.5

### Configuration

See above

### Are you willing to work on and submit a PR to address the issue?

- [X] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

### Code of Conduct

- [X] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

+"""The #2039 column restore is paid only when an alias can actually shadow a column.
+
+`_step_edges_with_source_columns` re-joins the WHOLE edge frame per step to undo an alias
+marker stamped over a column its own step filters on. That shadowing needs an edge alias NAMED
+like an edge column; paying the restore unconditionally cost LJ 1-hop +27% (34.7M-edge semi-join
+twice per hop). These pins hold the guard on both sides of that boundary.
+"""

+import pandas as pd
+import pytest
+
+import graphistry
+from graphistry.compute.ast import n, e_forward, e_undirected
+from graphistry.compute.gfql.lazy.engine.polars.chain import _edge_alias_can_shadow_column
+

+    nodes = pd.DataFrame({"node_id": [0, 1, 2]})
+    return graphistry.nodes(nodes, "node_id").edges(edges, "src", "dst")
+
+

+    ([n(), e_undirected(hops=1), n()], False),
+    ([n(), e_forward(), n()], False),
+    ([n(), e_forward(name="not_a_column"), n()], False),
+    # An alias named like an edge column CAN be stamped over it: the restore is required.
+    ([n(), e_forward(name="rel"), n()], True),
+    ([n(), e_forward(name="src"), n()], True),
+    ([n(), e_forward(name="dst"), n()], True),
+    # One colliding alias anywhere in the chain is enough.
+    ([n(), e_forward(name="safe"), n(), e_forward(name="rel"), n()], True),
+])
+def test_restore_is_required_exactly_when_an_alias_can_shadow_a_column(g, ops, expected):
+    assert _edge_alias_can_shadow_column(ops, g) is expected

+    assert _edge_alias_can_shadow_column([n(), e_forward(), n()], graphistry.bind()) is True
+
+
+def test_the_colliding_alias_chain_still_answers(g):
+    """The guard must not change what the collision case returns -- only whether the
+    restore is skipped for everyone else."""

+    assert out._nodes is not None and len(out._nodes) > 0

problem_statement.title: Bulk g.hop() regression: LJ 1-hop +27%, 2-hop +6%, disjoint ranges; entered during the 0.60 stack, not the perf PRs
problem_statement.body:
## What

Bulk traversal via `g.hop()` regressed measurably between `e951e9a2c` (2026-09-04) and current master. Found while re-measuring the GraphFrames ladder, whose staleness had been hiding it — **no board in CI or the release suite exercises this shape.**

LiveJournal (34.7M edges), polars, 50 seeds, `warmups=2 iters=5`, via `run_streaming_rung_dgx.sh` (perf lock, load gate, safe_run, breach classifier). 3 reps per arm, interleaved, one session, one container. **Result sizes identical in all 12 runs.**

| task | `e951e9a2c` | `f283a305e` (shipped) | ranges | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| filter | 24.2, 25.8, 24.5 | 24.4, 24.7, 24.9 | overlap | **flat** |
| **hop1** | 351.8, 259.5, 333.4 | 403.9, 423.2, 426.1 | **DISJOINT** (351.8 < 403.9) | **+26.9%** |
| **hop2** | 7211.0, 6895.5, 6915.9 | 7350.1, 7366.4, 7347.5 | **DISJOINT** (7211.0 < 7347.5) | **+6.3%** |

`filter` is the built-in control: same frames, same container, same I/O, no traversal — and it is flat. **Both traversal tasks regressed and only the traversal tasks regressed.**

## NOT caused by the 0.60 performance PRs

problem_statement.title: [Bug]: Lithium is not conserved with concentration-dependent particle diffusivity on a non-uniform particle mesh
problem_statement.body:
**PyBaMM Version:** 26.8.0.1.dev11+g861f9315c
**Python Version:** 3.12.11

### Describe the bug

When the particle submesh is non-uniform *and* the particle diffusivity depends on
concentration, the Fickian particle imposes the wrong surface flux, so lithium is
silently created or destroyed. On `ORegan2022` with an `Exponential1DSubMesh` and
`r_n = r_p = 16`, the cell **gains 26 % of its particle lithium over three 1C
cycles**. Nothing in the model reports a loss or gain — `Total lithium in
particles [mol]` simply drifts.

The error is a systematic multiplicative bias on the surface flux, applied in the
same direction on every intercalation step, so it accumulates monotonically rather
than averaging out. It is easy to mistake for a degradation signal: in a long
ageing run with LAM and SEI submodels active it shows up as `LLI [%]` that does
not reconcile with the model's own loss terms.

Both ingredients are required. Uniform mesh: exact. Constant diffusivity: exact.

#### Cause

`FickianDiffusion` sets the surface boundary condition as a *gradient*, dividing
the interfacial current by the **boundary value** of the diffusivity
(`fickian_diffusion.py:209`):

```python
f"{Domain} {phase_name}particle bc [mol.m-4]": -j * R_nondim / self.param.F / pybamm.surf(D_eff)
```

The flux that condition actually produces is `N = -D_eff * grad(c)`, where `D_eff`
is interpolated from nodes onto the surface **edge**. That interpolation is
`FiniteVolume.shift`'s `arithmetic_mean`, whose boundary rows are hard-coded
`[1.5, -0.5]` and `[-0.5, 1.5]` (`finite_volume.py:1551-1560`) — a linear
extrapolation that assumes **uniformly spaced nodes**. `pybamm.surf` extrapolates
using the real node positions.

On a uniform mesh the two agree identically, so the imposed flux is exactly `j/F`.
On a graded mesh they do not, and the imposed flux is off by
`D_node->edge / surf(D_eff)`.

Note that `harmonic_mean` in the same method already weights by the true
control-volume widths (`beta = dx1 / (dx1 + dx2)`); only `arithmetic_mean`
hard-codes uniform spacing.

### Steps to Reproduce

**1. Full cell, stock parameter sets.** Leak is the percentage drop in
`Total lithium in particles [mol]` over three 1C cycles (negative = lithium
created):

```python
import pybamm

def leak(pset, mesh, n_r=16):
    model = pybamm.lithium_ion.SPMe()
    st = model.default_submesh_types
    if mesh == "exponential":
        for dom in ("negative particle", "positive particle"):
            st[dom] = pybamm.MeshGenerator(
                pybamm.Exponential1DSubMesh, submesh_params={"side": "right"}
            )
    sol = pybamm.Simulation(
        model,
        parameter_values=pybamm.ParameterValues(pset),
        experiment=pybamm.Experiment(
            ["Discharge at 1C until 3.0V", "Charge at 1C until 4.2V"] * 3
        ),
        var_pts={"x_n": 8, "x_s": 8, "x_p": 8, "r_n": n_r, "r_p": n_r},
        submesh_types=st,
    ).solve(initial_soc=1.0)
    n = sol["Total lithium in particles [mol]"](sol.t)
    return 100 * (1 - n[-1] / n[0])

for pset in ("ORegan2022", "Ecker2015", "Chen2020"):
    for n_r in (16, 64):
        print(pset, n_r, leak(pset, "uniform", n_r), leak(pset, "exponential", n_r))
```

| parameter set | r_n | uniform % | exponential % |
|---|---|---|---|
| ORegan2022 | 16 | -0.0000 | **-25.9351** |
| ORegan2022 | 64 | 0.0000 | -0.3540 |
| Ecker2015 | 16 | 0.0000 | 0.4274 |
| Ecker2015 | 64 | -0.0000 | 0.0244 |
| Chen2020 (constant D) | 16 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| Chen2020 (constant D) | 64 | -0.0000 | 0.0000 |

**2. Minimal reproduction, no battery model.** Pure diffusion in a sphere with a
constant surface flux and `D` linear in `c`, using the same BC form the Fickian
particle uses. The exact answer is `d<c>/dt = -3*N_surf/R`:

```python
import numpy as np
import pybamm

R, j_over_F, T = 1e-5, 1e-7, 3600.0

for label, gen in [
    ("uniform", pybamm.Uniform1DSubMesh),
    ("exponential(right)", pybamm.MeshGenerator(
        pybamm.Exponential1DSubMesh, submesh_params={"side": "right"})),
]:
    for npts in (16, 48, 128):
        model = pybamm.BaseModel()
        c = pybamm.Variable("c", domain="negative particle")
        D = 1e-14 * (1 + 9 * c / 1000.0)
        model.rhs = {c: -pybamm.div(-D * pybamm.grad(c))}
        model.boundary_conditions = {
            c: {"left": (pybamm.Scalar(0), "Neumann"),
                "right": (-j_over_F / pybamm.surf(D), "Neumann")}
        }
        model.initial_conditions = {c: pybamm.Scalar(500.0)}
        model.variables = {"mean": pybamm.r_average(c)}

        r = pybamm.SpatialVariable(
            "r_n", domain=["negative particle"], coord_sys="spherical polar")
        geom = {"negative particle": {r: {"min": pybamm.Scalar(0), "max": pybamm.Scalar(R)}}}
        mesh = pybamm.Mesh(geom, {"negative particle": gen}, {r: npts})
        pybamm.Discretisation(
            mesh, {"negative particle": pybamm.FiniteVolume()}).process_model(model)

        sol = pybamm.IDAKLUSolver(rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-10).solve(model, np.linspace(0, T, 50))
        got = float(sol["mean"](T) - sol["mean"](0))
        exact = -3 * j_over_F * T / R
        print(label, npts, 100 * (got - exact) / exact)
```

| mesh | npts=16 | npts=48 | npts=128 |
|---|---|---|---|
| uniform | 0.000 % | 0.000 % | 0.000 % |
| exponential(right) | -0.002 % | -0.000 % | -0.000 % |

Uniform is exact at every resolution; graded is not, and converges under
refinement — i.e. it is discretisation error, not integration error. Tightening
the solver from `rtol=atol=1e-6` to `1e-9` changes the full-cell leak by less
than 0.001 points.

**3. The two extrapolations, compared directly.** This is the whole bug in one
number:

```python
import numpy as np
import pybamm

R = 1e-5
r = pybamm.SpatialVariable("r_n", domain=["negative particle"], coord_sys="spherical polar")
geom = {"negative particle": {r: {"min": pybamm.Scalar(0), "max": pybamm.Scalar(R)}}}

for label, gen in [
    ("uniform", pybamm.Uniform1DSubMesh),
    ("exponential(right)", pybamm.MeshGenerator(
        pybamm.Exponential1DSubMesh, submesh_params={"side": "right"})),
]:
    for npts in (16, 64):
        mesh = pybamm.Mesh(geom, {"negative particle": gen}, {r: npts})
        fv = pybamm.FiniteVolume()
        disc = pybamm.Discretisation(mesh, {"negative particle": fv})
        c = pybamm.Variable("c", domain="negative particle")
        disc.set_variable_slices([c])
        D = 1e-14 * (1 + 99 * c / 1000.0)
        y = 1000.0 * mesh["negative particle"].nodes / R
        surf_val = float(np.ravel(disc.process_symbol(pybamm.surf(D)).evaluate(y=y))[-1])
        edge_val = float(np.ravel(
            fv.node_to_edge(disc.process_symbol(D)).evaluate(y=y))[-1])
        print(label, npts, 100 * (edge_val / surf_val - 1))
```

| mesh | npts | surf(D) | node->edge D | imposed flux error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| uniform | 16 | 1.000000e-12 | 1.000000e-12 | 0.000 % |
| uniform | 64 | 1.000000e-12 | 1.000000e-12 | 0.000 % |
| exponential(right) | 16 | 1.000000e-12 | 1.000659e-12 | 0.066 % |
| exponential(right) | 64 | 1.000000e-12 | 1.000037e-12 | 0.004 % |

### Suggested fix

Make `arithmetic_mean`'s node-to-edge weights use the real node spacing, as
`harmonic_mean` already does, so that the interior weights are distance-weighted
and the boundary rows extrapolate from the true node positions. That would make
the interpolated edge value agree with `pybamm.surf` and restore conservation on
any mesh.

A narrower alternative is to have `FickianDiffusion` impose the flux directly
rather than as a gradient divided by `surf(D_eff)`, which removes the dependence
on the two extrapolations agreeing.

Happy to open a PR for either.

problem_statement.title: [QUESTION] Environment variable replacement requires `$ENV:` in the actual OS variable name
problem_statement.body:
### What is the question?

The `enable_environment_variable_replacement` feature flag is meant to let users reference environment variables in `parameter.yml` using a `$ENV:VAR_NAME` token.

However, the current implementation appears to require the actual OS environment variable to be named with the `$ENV:` prefix. This seems impractical: AFAIK, no shell or CI system will allow a variable name that starts with `$ENV:`. So, it's effectively unusable outside of manually poking `os.environ` in a Python wrapper.

Would it be better to keep the plain OS variable name (`VAR_NAME`) and use `$ENV:` only as the in-file token prefix? Or am I missing something?

### Context

We currently run fabric-cicd via the fabric-cli command `fab deploy`, so we can only use real OS environment variables—we cannot set keys on `os.environ` from a Python wrapper.

### Library Version

_No response_

### Operating System

Not applicable

### Have you checked the documentation?

- [x] I have searched existing GitHub issues
- [x] I have reviewed the fabric-cicd documentation

### Additional Information

_No response_

problem_statement.title: Improve user experience when cluster is too busy for everserver
problem_statement.body:
If the cluster is too busy to accomodate the submitted everest server then the user is left with the following text in the terminal after some minutes of waiting:

```
Adding everest server to queue ...
Failed to start the server
```

This can be improved, as in:
* We should state in the message which queue the server is submitted to
* We should say explicitly that there was a timeout, and what the timeout was

problem_statement.title: A config key written without a value is dropped, where git reads it as true
problem_statement.body:
`GitConfigParser` cannot read a key that appears with no `=`, which is valid git config and means true.

```ini
[flag]
	enabled
```

```
git config -f cfg --get flag.enabled              -> exit 0, empty output
git config -f cfg --type=bool --get flag.enabled  -> true
git config -f cfg --list                          -> flag.enabled
```

```python
>>> GitConfigParser("cfg", read_only=True).get_value("flag", "enabled")
NoOptionError
```

The key is not stored at all. `OPTCRE` requires `[:=]`, so the line does not match, and the branch at `git/config.py:589-594` swallows it:

```python
else:
    # Check if it's an option with no value - it's just ignored by git.
    if not self.OPTVALUEONLY.match(line):
```

The comment is the part I would fix first regardless of the rest: git does not ignore it. `--list` shows the key and `--type=bool` reads it as true. `OPTVALUEONLY` exists only to recognise these lines so they can be discarded without raising a `ParsingError`.

One constraint on any fix, which is why I am asking rather than sending a patch. git distinguishes a valueless key from an empty one, and they differ exactly where it matters:

```
[f]
	novalue        --get ''   --type=bool true
	empty =        --get ''   --type=bool false
```

So storing `""` for the valueless case would make it read as false, the opposite of git. Representing it needs something that `get_value` can render as `""` while the boolean path reads as true.

There is also a write-back question: such a key is currently dropped on a read-modify-write, and once it parses it would need to be written back without an `=`.

Happy to send the patch with tests if you tell me which representation you want; the write-back ripple is the reason I have not guessed.

Found with git 2.50.1 and GitPython at a9913c7.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5 (Claude Code), per the identification rule in CONTRIBUTING.md.

## Describe the bug
Unable to use `files.rsync` with `_sudo=True`.

## To Reproduce

Try running the following operation (replace paths):

```python
files.rsync(
    src="/path/to/host/dir",
    dest="/path/to/remote/dir",
    _sudo=True,
)
```

             )
 
+    def _pixel_data_as_little_endian(self, ds: "Dataset") -> Buffer:
+        """Return `ds`'s *Pixel Data* as little-endian ordered bytes.
+
+        Encoders require little-endian input, so *Pixel Data* read from an
+        *Explicit VR Big Endian* dataset has to be byte swapped first. Without
+        this the encoder reads every sample byte-reversed and encodes corrupt
+        pixel data without raising - a 16-bit value of 1 becomes 256.
+
+        Parameters
+        ----------
+        ds : pydicom.dataset.Dataset
+            The dataset supplying the pixel data.
+
+        Returns
+        -------
+        bytes | bytearray | memoryview
+            The pixel data, byte swapped if the dataset is big-endian encoded.
+        """
+        src = cast(Buffer, ds.PixelData)
+        file_meta = getattr(ds, "file_meta", None)
+        if getattr(file_meta, "TransferSyntaxUID", None) != ExplicitVRBigEndian:
+            return src
+
+        # 8-bit OW stores pairs of samples in 16-bit words. Normalize the
+        # complete value before slicing frames, which may contain odd samples.
+        nr_bytes = self.bits_allocated // 8
+        if self.bits_allocated == 8 and ds[0x7FE00010].VR == "OW":
+            nr_bytes = 2
+        if nr_bytes < 2 or len(src) % nr_bytes:
+            return src
+
+        # Swap symmetric byte positions within each sample
+        buffer = bytearray(src)
+        for left in range(nr_bytes // 2):
+            right = nr_bytes - 1 - left
+            buffer[left::nr_bytes], buffer[right::nr_bytes] = (
+                buffer[right::nr_bytes],
+                buffer[left::nr_bytes],
+            )
+
+        return bytes(buffer)
+
     @property
     def src(self) -> "Buffer | np.ndarray":
         """Return the buffer-like or :class:`numpy.ndarray` containing the pixel data."""  # noqa: E501

problem_statement.title: `Dataset.compress()` produces byte-swapped pixel data when source Transfer Syntax is Explicit VR Big Endian
problem_statement.body:
## Description

`Dataset.compress()` silently produces corrupted (byte-swapped) pixel data when compressing a dataset whose Transfer Syntax is Explicit VR Big Endian (`1.2.840.10008.1.2.2`). The resulting compressed file contains pixel values with swapped byte order, where a 16-bit value of `1` (`0x0001`) becomes `256` (`0x0100`).

The corruption is silent: no error, no warning. For lossless compression (JPEG 2000 Lossless), the round-trip pixel data does not match the original.

We're aware that Explicit VR Big Endian was retired from the DICOM Standard in 2006 (Supplement 98) and that conformant implementations are not required to support it. However, Big Endian files still exist in the wild, including legacy PACS exports and long-running research datasets hosted on platforms like [IDA/LONI](https://ida.loni.usc.edu). Since pydicom does read these files (and `pixel_array` decodes them correctly), we'd expect `compress()` to handle them as well.

## Cause

When no `arr` argument is passed, `compress()` appears to read the raw `PixelData` bytes without accounting for the source transfer syntax endianness. On a little-endian host the big-endian bytes are fed directly to the encoder, which interprets them as little-endian.

## Workaround

Passing `arr=ds.pixel_array` explicitly forces `compress()` through the pixel decoding pipeline, which correctly handles the `>u2` / `>i2` dtype:

```python
ds = pydicom.dcmread("bigendian_file.dcm")
ds.compress(JPEG2000Lossless, arr=ds.pixel_array, encoding_plugin="pylibjpeg")
```

This is not documented as a requirement. The [compression tutorial](https://github.com/pydicom/pydicom/blob/main/doc/tutorials/pixel_data/compressing.rst) only shows `arr` being used for creating new datasets or updating pixel data, not as a mandatory workaround for Big Endian sources. It's worth noting that `compress()` is a method on the very `Dataset` that already holds the correctly decoded `pixel_array`, so having to pass it back in explicitly to avoid silent corruption is surprising.

## Reproducer

Uses a public Big Endian DICOM from [neurolabusc/dcm_qa_ts](https://github.com/neurolabusc/dcm_qa_ts/blob/main/In/3.dcm):

```python
import numpy as np
import pydicom
from pydicom.filewriter import dcmwrite
from pydicom.uid import JPEG2000Lossless

ds = pydicom.dcmread("3.dcm")  # Explicit VR Big Endian
original_pixels = ds.pixel_array.copy()

# Compression yields neither error nor warning
ds.compress(JPEG2000Lossless, generate_instance_uid=False)
dcmwrite("/tmp/compressed.dcm", ds)

# Round-trip check — FAILS
ds_comp = pydicom.dcmread("/tmp/compressed.dcm")
np.testing.assert_array_equal(original_pixels, ds_comp.pixel_array)
# AssertionError: Mismatched elements: 140956 / 147456 (95.6%)
```

## Environment

- pydicom 3.0.2
- Python 3.11
- Platform: little-endian (x86_64)

 These constraints are set in the function `define_total_supply_constraints()`.
 
+## Voltage Angle Limits
+
+AC lines and transformers can limit the magnitude of their linearised voltage angle difference to $\bar{\theta}$ (attribute `v_ang_max` in degrees). The limit applies symmetrically to both flow directions; the attribute `v_ang_min` is deprecated and ignored. The limit is imposed as a bound on the flow by dividing through the strictly positive $x^\text{pu,eff}$, and is only added for branches with a finite `v_ang_max`. Unlike a manual conversion into `s_max_pu`, this formulation contains no $s^\text{nom}$ and therefore stays linear for extendable branches, although the reactance is a fixed parameter in the optimisation (see [`n.optimize.optimize_transmission_expansion_iteratively()`][pypsa.optimization.OptimizationAccessor.optimize_transmission_expansion_iteratively]).
+
+For a line the angle difference is $\theta_{l,t} = x^\text{pu,eff}_l \, p_{l,t}$. For a transformer it additionally includes the phase shift $\phi_{t,t}$ (either the fixed `phase_shift` or, when `phase_shift_min < phase_shift_max`, the optimised phase-shift variable), so $\theta_{t,t} = x^\text{pu,eff}_t \, p_{t,t} + \phi_{t,t}$.
+
+| Constraint | Name |
+|-------------------|------------------|
+| $p_{l,t} \geq -\bar{\theta}_l / x^\text{pu,eff}_l$ | `Line-v_ang-lower` |
+| $p_{l,t} \leq \bar{\theta}_l / x^\text{pu,eff}_l$ | `Line-v_ang-upper` |
+| $p_{t,t} + \phi_{t,t} / x^\text{pu,eff}_t \geq -\bar{\theta}_t / x^\text{pu,eff}_t$ | `Transformer-v_ang-lower` |
+| $p_{t,t} + \phi_{t,t} / x^\text{pu,eff}_t \leq \bar{\theta}_t / x^\text{pu,eff}_t$ | `Transformer-v_ang-upper` |
+
+These constraints are set in the function `define_voltage_angle_constraints()`. For background on voltage angle difference limits, see the [MATPOWER manual](https://matpower.org/docs/MATPOWER-manual.pdf), pages 76-77.
+

+def define_voltage_angle_constraints(n: Network, sns: pd.Index) -> None:
+    """Define voltage angle difference limits for lines and transformers.
+
+    Caps the magnitude of the linearised voltage angle difference across each
+    AC line and transformer to ``v_ang_max`` (in degrees). The difference
+    equals ``x_pu_eff * s`` for lines and ``x_pu_eff * s + phase_shift`` for
+    transformers, so the limit becomes a symmetric bound after dividing
+    through the strictly positive ``x_pu_eff``:
+
+    -deg2rad(v_ang_max) / x_pu_eff <= s + phase_shift / x_pu_eff <= deg2rad(v_ang_max) / x_pu_eff
+
+    A fixed ``phase_shift`` shifts the flow bounds; an optimised phase shift
+    (``phase_shift_min < phase_shift_max``) enters the constraint as a variable.
+    Constraints are only created for assets with a finite ``v_ang_max``. The
+    deprecated ``v_ang_min`` is ignored; ``v_ang_max`` applies symmetrically.
+
+    See the MATPOWER manual (https://matpower.org/docs/MATPOWER-manual.pdf),
+    pages 76-77, for background on voltage angle difference limits.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    n : pypsa.Network
+        Network instance containing the model and component data
+    sns : pd.Index
+        Set of snapshots for which to define the constraints
+
+    """
+    model_sns = n.optimize._window.subset(sns).model_index
+
+    for c_name in ("Line", "Transformer"):
+        c = as_components(n, c_name)
+        static = c.static
+
+        if isfinite(static["v_ang_min"]).any():
+            warnings.warn(
+                f"The `v_ang_min` attribute of {c_name} is deprecated and "
+                "ignored. `v_ang_max` applies symmetrically as an absolute "
+                "voltage angle difference limit.",
+                DeprecationWarning,
+                stacklevel=2,
+            )
+
+        assets_i = static.index[isfinite(static["v_ang_max"])].intersection(
+            c.active_assets
+        )
+        if c_name == "Line":
+            assets_i = assets_i[static.loc[assets_i, "carrier"] == "AC"]
+        if assets_i.empty:
+            continue
+
+        x_pu_eff = c.da["x_pu_eff"].sel(name=assets_i)
+        cap = c.da["v_ang_max"].sel(name=assets_i) * DEG2RAD / x_pu_eff
+        s = n.model[f"{c_name}-s"].sel(name=assets_i, snapshot=model_sns)
+        active = c.da.active.sel(name=assets_i, snapshot=model_sns)
+
+        if c_name == "Line":
+            n.model.add_constraints(s, ">=", -cap, name="Line-v_ang-lower", mask=active)
+            n.model.add_constraints(s, "<=", cap, name="Line-v_ang-upper", mask=active)
+            continue
+
+        varying = (
+            static.loc[assets_i, "phase_shift_min"]
+            < static.loc[assets_i, "phase_shift_max"]
+        )
+        fixed_i = assets_i[~varying]
+        var_i = assets_i[varying]
+
+        if not fixed_i.empty:
+            offset = (
+                DEG2RAD
+                * c.da["phase_shift"].sel(name=fixed_i, snapshot=model_sns)
+                / x_pu_eff.sel(name=fixed_i)
+            )
+            lhs = s.sel(name=fixed_i)
+            mask = active.sel(name=fixed_i)
+            n.model.add_constraints(
+                lhs,
+                ">=",
+                -cap.sel(name=fixed_i) - offset,
+                name="Transformer-v_ang-lower",
+                mask=mask,
+            )
+            n.model.add_constraints(
+                lhs,
+                "<=",
+                cap.sel(name=fixed_i) - offset,
+                name="Transformer-v_ang-upper",
+                mask=mask,
+            )
+
+        if not var_i.empty:
+            ps = n.model["Transformer-phase_shift"].sel(name=var_i, snapshot=model_sns)
+            lhs = s.sel(name=var_i) + ps * (DEG2RAD / x_pu_eff.sel(name=var_i))
+            mask = active.sel(name=var_i)
+            cap_var = cap.sel(name=var_i)
+            n.model.add_constraints(
+                lhs, ">=", -cap_var, name="Transformer-v_ang-var-lower", mask=mask
+            )
+            n.model.add_constraints(
+                lhs, "<=", cap_var, name="Transformer-v_ang-var-upper", mask=mask
+            )
+

problem_statement.title: More forms of `Line` limits
problem_statement.body:
- enforced limits on voltage angle differences (directly translate to `s_nom = 1/x_pu_eff * angle_diff`).

- TATL, Temporary Admissible Transmission Loading, see https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.06667 (temporarily higher line loading `delta_s_nom`, which has constraint energy over set period of time).

- example of dynamic line rating (`s_max_pu > 0`).

- example of approximation of N-1 (`s_max_pu = 0.7)`

--- a/CHANGELOG.md

@@ -71,6 +71,7 @@ All notable changes to CrossTL are documented in this file.
 
 ### Fixed
 
+- DirectX lowers canonical Metal `fabs`, `fmin`, and `fmax` to native intrinsics and preserves `select(falseValue, trueValue, condition)` argument order, scalar/vector result types, and eager evaluation. Source-defined helpers remain ordinary calls; unresolved or non-Boolean selection conditions and shadowed target intrinsics produce structured diagnostics. Required Windows readbacks cover finite values, NaNs, infinities, and both selection branches.
 - Historical and current-pinned MLX FFT HLSL evidence now reflects C++ integer promotion of all 20 native-16 shift counts, with refreshed deterministic artifact identities and an explicit structural regression.
 - Current-pinned multidimensional MLX GEMV no longer relies on WARP physical-wave lane topology: its DirectX reduction now uses deterministic logical 32-lane software subgroups, fixing the observed replacement of logical lanes 5–8 by physical lanes 21–24.
 - DirectX native 16-bit Metal `as_type` lowering uses exact `asfloat16`/`asint16`/`asuint16` reinterpretation by default; an explicit source-scoped widening mode reconstructs binary16 payloads with integer IEEE-754 masks and keeps logical `float16_t` arithmetic, sign application, returns, and consumers in float32. Scalar native `int16_t`/`uint16_t` arithmetic now also follows Metal/C++ integer promotion before shifts, preventing FP8 scale-bit construction from truncating `<< 23` to a 16-bit shift and eliminating current-pinned MXFP4’s signed-zero collapse on WARP.

+"""DirectX lowering of canonical Metal math and eager selection."""
+
+import json
+import math
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+
+from crosstl import translate
+from crosstl.backend.DirectX.DirectxCrossGLCodeGen import HLSLSelectOverloadError
+from crosstl.project.native_runtime_drivers import DirectXComputeRuntime
+from crosstl.project.runtime_verification import (
+    NativeRuntimeBufferBinding,
+    NativeRuntimeDispatchRequest,
+    RuntimeDispatchGeometry,
+    RuntimeResourceBinding,
+)
+from crosstl.translator import parse
+from crosstl.translator.ast import FunctionCallNode
+from crosstl.translator.codegen.directx_codegen import (
+    DirectXContextualConversionError,
+    HLSLCodeGen,
+)
+from tests.test_translator.test_codegen.test_directx_codegen import (
+    assert_directx_warnings_clean_if_available,
+)
+
+REQUIRE_RUNTIME_ENV = "CROSTL_REQUIRE_DIRECTX_METAL_MATH"
+SOURCE = """
+#include <metal_stdlib>
+using namespace metal;
+
+float record(thread float& counter, float value) {
+    counter += 1.0f;
+    return value;
+}
+
+kernel void math_probe(
+    device const float* values [[buffer(0)]],
+    device float* results [[buffer(1)]],
+    uint i [[thread_position_in_grid]]) {
+    float x = values[2 * i];
+    float y = values[2 * i + 1];
+    results[8 * i] = metal::fabs(x);
+    results[8 * i + 1] = metal::fmin(x, y);
+    results[8 * i + 2] = metal::fmax(x, y);
+    results[8 * i + 3] = metal::select(x, y, i % 2 == 0);
+    float2 selected = metal::select(float2(x, y), float2(y, x), bool2(true, false));
+    results[8 * i + 4] = selected.x;
+    results[8 * i + 5] = selected.y;
+    float left_count = 0.0f;
+    float right_count = 0.0f;
+    results[8 * i + 6] = metal::select(record(left_count, x), record(right_count, y), false);
+    results[8 * i + 7] = left_count + right_count;
+}
+"""
+
+
+def _translate(tmp_path):
+    source = tmp_path / "math.metal"
+    source.write_text(SOURCE, encoding="utf-8")
+    return translate(str(source), backend="directx", format_output=False)
+
+
+def test_metal_math_translates_and_compiles_for_directx(tmp_path):
+    generated = _translate(tmp_path)
+    assert "abs(x)" in generated
+    assert "min(x, y)" in generated
+    assert "max(x, y)" in generated
+    assert "select(((i % 2) == 0), y, x)" in generated
+    assert "select(bool2(true, false), float2(y, x), float2(x, y))" in generated
+    assert_directx_warnings_clean_if_available(generated, tmp_path)
+
+
+def test_directx_nested_metal_math_preserves_result_types(tmp_path):
+    source = """
+    shader NestedMath {
+        float stableHypot(float x, float y) {
+            float a = fmax(fabs(x), fabs(y));
+            float b = fmin(fabs(x), fabs(y));
+            float r = (b / a) * (b / a);
+            float h1 = sqrt(2.0) * a;
+            float h2 = a + (a * r) / 2.0;
+            float h3 = a * sqrt(1.0 + r);
+            bool first = a == b;
+            bool second = sqrt(1.0 + r) == 1.0 && r > 0.0;
+            return select(select(h3, h2, second), h1, first);
+        }
+        RWStructuredBuffer<float> results @ binding(0);
+        compute {
+            layout(local_size_x = 1) in;
+            void main(uvec3 index @ gl_GlobalInvocationID) {
+                results[index.x] = stableHypot(float(index.x), 2.0);
+                ivec2 result = select(ivec2(1), ivec2(2), select(bvec2(false), bvec2(true), bvec2(true, false)));
+                results[index.x + 1u] = float(result.x);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    """
+    generated = HLSLCodeGen().generate(parse(source))
+    assert "max(abs(x), abs(y))" in generated
+    assert "return select(first, h1, select(second, h2, h3));" in generated
+    assert_directx_warnings_clean_if_available(generated, tmp_path)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("vector", [False, True])
+def test_hlsl_select_roundtrip_retains_hlsl_argument_order(tmp_path, vector):
+    result_type = "float2" if vector else "float"
+    condition = "bool2(true, false)" if vector else "false"
+    source = tmp_path / "selection.hlsl"
+    source.write_text(
+        f"""RWStructuredBuffer<{result_type}> results : register(u0);
+        [numthreads(1, 1, 1)]
+        void main(uint3 id : SV_DispatchThreadID) {{
+            results[id.x] = select({condition}, {result_type}(20.0), {result_type}(10.0));
+        }}""",
+        encoding="utf-8",
+    )
+    intermediate = translate(str(source), backend="crossgl", format_output=False)
+    assert "select(" in intermediate
+    generated = translate(str(source), backend="directx", format_output=False)
+    assert f"select({condition}," in generated
+    assert_directx_warnings_clean_if_available(generated, tmp_path)
+
+
+def test_hlsl_select_roundtrip_preserves_source_helper(tmp_path):
+    source = tmp_path / "helper.hlsl"
+    source.write_text(
+        """float select(float x, float y, float z, float w) { return x - y + z + w; }
+        RWStructuredBuffer<float> results : register(u0);
+        [numthreads(1, 1, 1)]
+        void main() { results[0] = select(10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0); }
+        """,
+        encoding="utf-8",
+    )
+    intermediate = translate(str(source), backend="crossgl", format_output=False)
+    assert "select(10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0)" in intermediate
+    generated = translate(str(source), backend="directx", format_output=False)
+    assert "select_(10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0)" in generated
+    assert_directx_warnings_clean_if_available(generated, tmp_path)
+
+
+def test_hlsl_select_rejects_ambiguous_source_overload(tmp_path):
+    source = tmp_path / "ambiguous.hlsl"
+    source.write_text(
+        """float select(float x, float y, float z) { return x - y + z; }
+        RWStructuredBuffer<float> results : register(u0);
+        [numthreads(1, 1, 1)]
+        void main() { results[0] = select(10.0, 20.0, 30.0); }
+        """,
+        encoding="utf-8",
+    )
+    with pytest.raises(HLSLSelectOverloadError) as error:
+        translate(str(source), backend="directx", format_output=False)
+    assert error.value.reason == "select-overload-ownership-unresolved"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "expression,expected",
+    [
+        ("fabs(vec2(1.0))", "vec2"),
+        ("fmin(vec2(1.0), vec2(2.0))", "vec2"),
+        ("fmax(vec2(1.0), vec2(2.0))", "vec2"),
+        ("select(ivec2(1), ivec2(2), bvec2(true))", "ivec2"),
+        ("select(false, true, true)", "bool"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_directx_metal_math_result_type(expression, expected):
+    ast = parse(f"shader ResultType {{ {expected} f() {{ return {expression}; }} }}")
+    call = next(node for node in ast.walk() if isinstance(node, FunctionCallNode))
+    assert HLSLCodeGen().expression_result_type(call) == expected
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "name,arity", [("fabs", 1), ("fmin", 2), ("fmax", 2), ("select", 3)]
+)
+def test_directx_metal_math_preserves_source_helpers(tmp_path, name, arity):
+    parameters = ", ".join(f"float a{i}" for i in range(arity))
+    arguments = ", ".join(f"{i}.0" for i in range(arity))
+    source = f"""
+        shader SourceHelper {{
+            float {name}({parameters}) {{ return a0 + 10.0; }}
+            RWStructuredBuffer<float> results @ binding(0);
+            compute {{
+                layout(local_size_x = 1) in;
+                void main() {{ results[0] = {name}({arguments}); }}
+            }}
+        }}
+    """
+    generated = HLSLCodeGen().generate(parse(source))
+    target_name = "select_" if name == "select" else name
+    assert f"float {target_name}({parameters})" in generated
+    assert f"results[0] = {target_name}({arguments});" in generated
+    assert_directx_warnings_clean_if_available(generated, tmp_path)
+
+
+def test_directx_source_select_alias_avoids_existing_names(tmp_path):
+    ast = parse("""shader SelectNames {
+        float select(float x, float y, bool choose) { return choose ? y : x; }
+        float select_(float value) { return value + 1.0; }
+        RWStructuredBuffer<float> results @ binding(0);
+        compute {
+            layout(local_size_x = 1) in;
+            void main() {
+                float select__ = 3.0;
+                results[0] = select(select_(1.0), select__, false);
+            }
+        }
+    }""")
+    generated = HLSLCodeGen().generate(ast)
+    assert "float select___(float x, float y, bool choose)" in generated
+    assert "results[0] = select___(select_(1.0), select__, false);" in generated
+    assert_directx_warnings_clean_if_available(generated, tmp_path)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "name,target,arity", [("fabs", "abs", 1), ("fmin", "min", 2), ("fmax", "max", 2)]
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("binding", ["function", "local", "global"])
+def test_directx_metal_math_rejects_shadowed_target(name, target, arity, binding):
+    parameters = ", ".join(f"float a{i}" for i in range(arity))
+    arguments = ", ".join("1.0" for _ in range(arity))
+    declaration = f"float {target}({parameters}) {{ return 99.0; }}"
+    global_declaration = (
+        declaration
+        if binding == "function"
+        else (f"float {target} = 99.0;" if binding == "global" else "")
+    )
+    local_declaration = f"float {target} = 99.0;" if binding == "local" else ""
+    ast = parse(f"""shader ShadowedTarget {{
+        {global_declaration}
+        float probe() {{ {local_declaration} return {name}({arguments}); }}
+    }}""")
+    with pytest.raises(DirectXContextualConversionError) as error:
+        HLSLCodeGen().generate(ast)
+    assert error.value.reason == "metal-math-target-shadowed"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "condition,reason",
+    [
+        ("2.0", "select-condition-not-boolean"),
+        ("ivec2(0, -1)", "select-condition-not-boolean"),
+        ("unknownCondition()", "select-condition-unresolved"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_directx_select_rejects_unproven_condition(condition, reason):
+    ast = parse(f"""shader InvalidSelect {{
+        float probe() {{ return select(1.0, 2.0, {condition}); }}
+    }}""")
+    call = next(node for node in ast.walk() if isinstance(node, FunctionCallNode))
+    call.source_location = {"line": 2, "column": 32}
+    with pytest.raises(DirectXContextualConversionError) as error:
+        HLSLCodeGen().generate(ast)
+    assert error.value.reason == reason
+    assert error.value.source_location == call.source_location
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "expression", ["fabs()", "fmin(1.0)", "fmax(1.0)", "select(1.0, 2.0)"]
+)
+def test_directx_metal_math_rejects_invalid_arity(expression):
+    with pytest.raises(DirectXContextualConversionError) as error:
+        HLSLCodeGen().generate(
+            parse(f"shader Arity {{ float f() {{ return {expression}; }} }}")
+        )
+    assert error.value.reason == "metal-math-invalid-arity"
+
+
+def test_directx_metal_math_executes(tmp_path):
+    if os.environ.get(REQUIRE_RUNTIME_ENV) != "1":
+        pytest.skip(f"set {REQUIRE_RUNTIME_ENV}=1 to require native Direct3D execution")
+    assert sys.platform == "win32", "Native Direct3D checks require Windows"
+    compiler = shutil.which("dxc")
+    assert compiler is not None, "DXC is required"
+    generated = _translate(tmp_path)
+    artifact = tmp_path / "math.hlsl"
+    module = tmp_path / "math.dxil"
+    artifact.write_text(generated, encoding="utf-8")
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        [
+            compiler,
+            "-T",
+            "cs_6_6",
+            "-E",
+            "CSMain",
+            "-WX",
+            str(artifact),
+            "-Fo",
+            str(module),
+        ],
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        timeout=60,
+    )
+    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stdout + result.stderr
+    pairs = [
+        (3.0, -4.0),
+        (-2.0, 5.0),
+        (math.nan, 7.0),
+        (7.0, math.nan),
+        (-math.inf, math.inf),
+        (math.inf, -math.inf),
+        (math.nan, math.nan),
+    ]
+    expected = []
+    for index, (x, y) in enumerate(pairs):
+        minimum = y if math.isnan(x) else (x if math.isnan(y) else min(x, y))
+        maximum = y if math.isnan(x) else (x if math.isnan(y) else max(x, y))
+        expected.extend(
+            [abs(x), minimum, maximum, y if index % 2 == 0 else x, y, y, x, 2.0]
+        )
+    buffers = {}
+    for name, binding, values, count in (
+        ("values", 0, [value for pair in pairs for value in pair], len(pairs) * 2),
+        ("results", 1, None, len(expected)),
+    ):
+        output = values is None
+        buffers[name] = NativeRuntimeBufferBinding(
+            name=name,
+            binding=RuntimeResourceBinding(
+                name=name,
+                kind="buffer",
+                type_name=("RW" if output else "") + "StructuredBuffer<float>",
+                set=0,
+                binding=binding,
+                access="read_write" if output else "read",
+            ),
+            source="expectedOutput" if output else "input",
+            dtype="float32",
+            shape=(count,),
+            value=values,
+        )
+    request = NativeRuntimeDispatchRequest(
+        target="directx",
+        artifact={"target": "directx"},
+        artifact_path=artifact,
+        module_path=module,
+        loaded_artifact=module.read_bytes(),
+        buffers=buffers,
+        constants={},
+        entry_point="CSMain",
+        dispatch=RuntimeDispatchGeometry(
+            entry_point="CSMain",
+            workgroup_size=(1, 1, 1),
+            workgroup_count=(len(pairs), 1, 1),
+        ),
+    )
+    runtime = DirectXComputeRuntime()
+    availability = runtime.is_available(None, None)
+    assert availability.available, availability.reason
+    outputs = runtime.dispatch(None, None, request)
+    (tmp_path / "outputs.json").write_text(
+        json.dumps(outputs, indent=2), encoding="utf-8"
+    )
+    actual = outputs["results"]["values"]
+    assert len(actual) == len(expected)
+    for observed, reference in zip(actual, expected):
+        assert math.isnan(observed) if math.isnan(reference) else observed == reference

@@ -46,6 +46,7 @@ All notable changes to CrossTL are documented in this file.
 
 ### Improved
 
+- Metal entry discovery reuses the preprocessor's bounded interval index for comment and literal exclusions, avoiding repeated linear scans while preserving entry ordering, locations, provenance and unresolved-name diagnostics.
 - Metal round trips restore brace initialization for unshadowed aggregate calls, accept integral reference values in pointer-offset assignments, and resolve constrained free-function templates before unconstrained helper specialization. Enabled SFINAE fallbacks materialize concretely, disabled fallbacks leave native overload calls intact, and unknown or ambiguous resolutions fail closed. Generated fallback helpers avoid collisions with source identifiers without changing ordinary calls.
 - Metal round trips now resolve and elide source typedef chains, map native bfloat values and result reconstruction, materialize constrained free operators with source-compatible overload selection, infer concrete aggregate aliases, recognize branch-complete returns, preserve narrow `as_type` storage, and admit only proven read-only immediate scalar-parameter views as matching thread-local single-field aggregates while every other unimplemented pointer reinterpretation remains fail-closed. Dependent free-operator calls rebind only to previously emitted exact helpers; known contextual aggregate conversions use only non-explicit constructors; 64-bit vectors map to native Metal types; bfloat minimum/maximum arguments promote safely; and discarded type constructors plus Boolean relational promotions remain warning-fatal native-compiler safe.
 - Selected-entry target capability validation now inspects only the reachable scoped AST before code generation, so unrelated declarations cannot block an otherwise valid DirectX, Metal, or OpenGL artifact while reachable unsupported operations still fail closed.

problem_statement.title: Index excluded source intervals during Metal entry discovery
problem_statement.body:
## Problem

Metal entry discovery checks every candidate position against an entire interval list with `_position_in_spans`:

```python
return any(start <= position < end for start, end in spans)
```

This repeats a linear scan for each entry and unresolved-host-name candidate. Macro-expanded files with many string literals or excluded declarations therefore spend substantial time on interval membership rather than discovering entries.

## Evidence

Implementation: `662748e3a37e9daec80eff69120f39e050597ea3`, `crosstl/backend/Metal/preprocessor.py`, `_position_in_spans`, `_unresolved_metal_host_name_diagnostics`, and `discover_metal_entry_points`.

A profile of the public runtime manifest builder for one `ss_Powercomplex64` artifact at MLX `d9add9d11f3154111a4c85f267ec2fd307ecd18e` invokes entry discovery four times. The discovery itself can also be reproduced directly:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from crosstl.translator.source_registry import SOURCE_REGISTRY, register_default_sources

root = Path("/path/to/pinned/mlx")
source = root / "mlx/backend/metal/kernels/binary.metal"
register_default_sources()
discovery = SOURCE_REGISTRY.get("metal").discover_entry_points(
    source.read_text(), file_path=str(source), include_paths=[str(root)]
)
assert not discovery.diagnostics
```

Across four discoveries, `cProfile` records:

- 32,988 `_position_in_spans` calls, 84.65 cumulative seconds.
- 410,221,528 membership-generator evaluations, 40.42 seconds in the generator alone.
- 158.51 cumulative seconds across the four full discovery calls.

Measurements are from Python 3.14.7 / Apple M2 Max under concurrent test load and include profiler overhead. The algorithmic call counts are the main evidence; no wall-time threshold is proposed for CI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Build a reusable interval index or equivalent membership structure once per relevant source/span collection, instead of linearly scanning every interval for every candidate.
- Preserve the exact half-open `start <= position < end` behavior, including boundaries, empty lists, adjacent, duplicate, nested and overlapping intervals. Do not assume concatenated exclusion lists are already sorted or disjoint.
- Preserve entry order, names, locations, provenance, stages and all unresolved-name diagnostics. Comment/literal/template-only false positives fixed in #1863 must not return.
- Bound index lifetime to the corresponding source and retain source-option/include/define isolation.
- Add deterministic complexity-oriented tests and cold/warm discovery equivalence on representative large generated fixtures and the pinned corpus.

This is a general Metal discovery cost exposed by MLX, not an MLX-specific fast path. It is related to #1971 but distinct from caching function/type discovery during template materialization.

+++ b/aqua/core/intake_drivers/xarray/xzarr.py
@@ -6,6 +6,34 @@
 from .readers import TolerantXArrayDatasetReader
 
 
+def _relax_s3_bucket_name_validation():
+    """Drop botocore's AWS-only bucket-name validator from its builtin handlers.
+
+    Some S3-compatible object stores used for AQUA zarr sources (e.g. LUMI-O) use bucket
+    names containing a colon, which are invalid on real AWS: botocore's built-in
+    ``validate_bucket_name`` handler rejects the request before it is even sent. Removing
+    the entry from ``BUILTIN_HANDLERS`` (read by every new (aio)botocore ``Session``, as
+    created internally by s3fs on every filesystem instantiation) disables that check
+    process-wide; the actual S3-compatible endpoint still validates the bucket itself.
+    """
+    try:
+        from botocore import handlers as botocore_handlers
+    except ImportError:
+        return
+    botocore_handlers.BUILTIN_HANDLERS = [
+        entry for entry in botocore_handlers.BUILTIN_HANDLERS if entry[1] is not botocore_handlers.validate_bucket_name
+    ]
+
+
+_relax_s3_bucket_name_validation()
+
+
+def _is_fsspec_urlpath(urlpath):
+    """Return True if urlpath (str or list of str) carries an fsspec protocol (e.g. ``s3://``)."""
+    paths = urlpath if isinstance(urlpath, (list, tuple, set)) else [urlpath]
+    return any(isinstance(p, str) and "://" in p for p in paths)
+
+
 class IntakeZarrSource(IntakeXarraySourceAdapter):
     """Open one or more Zarr stores with xarray, registered as the ``zarr`` driver.
 
@@ -37,6 +65,11 @@ def __init__(self, urlpath, storage_options=None, metadata=None, xarray_kwargs=N
         if "chunks" not in xarray_kwargs:
             kwargs.setdefault("chunks", {})
 
+        # zarr rejects storage_options on a plain local-path store: it is only honoured
+        # when the store is opened as an fsspec URI, so drop it for local urlpaths
+        if storage_options and not _is_fsspec_urlpath(urlpath):
+            storage_options = None
+
         data = readers.datatypes.Zarr(urlpath, storage_options=storage_options, metadata=metadata)
         self.reader = TolerantXArrayDatasetReader(data, **xarray_kwargs, metadata=metadata, **kwargs)
         super().__init__(data, xarray_kwargs, metadata)

problem_statement.title: [Backend] Allow Lumi-O s3 bucket access
problem_statement.body:
We have now LRA in zarr format on Lumi-O buckets.
The bucket name contains the project number with semicolumns, this is not a valid bucket name for botocore, which raise an error, for this reason a workaround is needed. 

After the merge of the new intake xarray drive #2958 we will add to the `intake_drivers/xarray/xzarr.py` file:

```python
def _relax_s3_bucket_name_validation():
    """Drop botocore's AWS-only bucket-name validator from its builtin handlers.

    Some S3-compatible object stores used for AQUA zarr sources (e.g. LUMI-O) use bucket
    names containing a colon, which are invalid on real AWS: botocore's built-in
    ``validate_bucket_name`` handler rejects the request before it is even sent. Removing
    the entry from ``BUILTIN_HANDLERS`` (read by every new (aio)botocore ``Session``, as
    created internally by s3fs on every filesystem instantiation) disables that check
    process-wide; the actual S3-compatible endpoint still validates the bucket itself.
    """
    try:
        from botocore import handlers as botocore_handlers
    except ImportError:
        return
    botocore_handlers.BUILTIN_HANDLERS = [
        entry for entry in botocore_handlers.BUILTIN_HANDLERS if entry[1] is not botocore_handlers.validate_bucket_name
    ]


_relax_s3_bucket_name_validation()
```

title: fix(copy): keep frozen constraints frozen in Model.copy
issue_title: Model.copy() turns frozen CSRConstraints into dense Constraints

install_config.install: pip install -e ".[dev]"

gold_patch:
diff --git a/doc/release_notes.rst b/doc/release_notes.rst
index d3ff4dd83..dccad9b82 100644
--- a/doc/release_notes.rst
+++ b/doc/release_notes.rst
@@ -81,6 +81,7 @@ Upcoming Version
 * ``CSRConstraint.loc``, ``update`` and ``from_rule``, and assigning to ``coeffs``, ``vars`` or ``sign``, now raise an ``AttributeError`` saying the operation is not supported on a frozen constraint and naming ``.mutable()`` as the way out (for ``from_rule``: build with ``Constraint.from_rule`` and ``.freeze()`` the result), like the read-only ``rhs``, ``lhs`` and ``scaling`` setters, instead of a bare ``AttributeError``. (`#963 <https://github.com/PyPSA/linopy/issues/963>`__)
 * ``linopy.merge`` with ``join="outer"``, ``"left"`` or ``"right"`` no longer raises an xarray ``MergeError`` when only one operand carries an auxiliary coordinate on a joined dimension. The constant was reindexed with a fill value of ``0`` that was also written into the auxiliary coordinate, so it no longer matched the coefficients' copy. The coordinate now follows its rows onto the joined grid and is NaN where no operand provides it, under both semantics. The same holds for ``.add`` / ``.sub`` / ``.mul`` / ``.div`` with a constant and a reindexing ``join=``.
 * A frozen constraint caches the label-to-position mapping of its matrix columns by weak reference and only rebuilds it when the constraint or the set of variables changes. While a persistent snapshot holds the arrays, repeated matrix assembly on an unchanged model returns the same objects, so the snapshot diff can again skip the comparison of untouched frozen constraints by object identity; one-off exports such as ``to_file`` retain no extra memory. (`#933 <https://github.com/PyPSA/linopy/issues/933>`__)
+* ``Model.copy`` (and the ``copy.copy``/``copy.deepcopy`` protocols) keeps frozen constraints as ``CSRConstraint`` instead of rebuilding them as dense ``Constraint``; ``deep=True`` copies their arrays, and duals are copied only with ``include_solution=True``. A CSR-backed objective is now deep-copied with ``deep=True`` as well. The auxiliary coordinates of a CSR grid are stored read-only, so a copy can share them safely. (`#981 <https://github.com/PyPSA/linopy/issues/981>`__)
 * ``Solver.close()`` no longer leaves dangling native handles behind. The solver model is now dropped before the environment that owns it, instead of after. And the COPT and MindOpt file interfaces no longer hand back a model they already disposed: after a file-based COPT or MindOpt solve, ``model.solver_model`` is ``None`` rather than a handle into freed memory. (`#899 <https://github.com/PyPSA/linopy/pull/899>`__)
 
 **Breaking Changes**

     indexes: dict[str, pd.Index]
     aux: AuxCoords = field(default_factory=dict)
 
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        object.__setattr__(
+            self, "aux", {n: (d, _readonly(v)) for n, (d, v) in self.aux.items()}
+        )
+
     @classmethod
     def from_coords(cls, coords: Iterable[pd.Index]) -> Grid:
         """Build from one index per dimension, each named after its dim."""
@@ -749,6 +754,15 @@ def _densify_notice(reason: str) -> None:
         )
 
 
+def _readonly(values: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+    """``values`` as a read-only array, copied first if it is writable."""
+    if not values.flags.writeable:
+        return values
+    values = values.copy()
+    values.setflags(write=False)
+    return values
+
+

     """Scalar and one-dimensional auxiliary coordinates of ``ds`` lying on ``dims``."""
     aux: AuxCoords = {}

problem_statement.title: Model.copy() turns frozen CSRConstraints into dense Constraints
problem_statement.body:
<!-- Replace this line with your own intent and motivation, by hand. -->

> [!NOTE]
> The following content was generated by AI.

### Version Checks (indicate both or one)

- [ ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the lastest [release](https://github.com/pypsa/linopy/releases) of Linopy.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the current [`master`](https://github.com/pypsa/linopy/tree/master) branch of Linopy.

### Issue Description

`Model.copy()` turns every frozen `CSRConstraint` into a dense `Constraint`, while the copy keeps `freeze_constraints=True`. The copy is therefore no longer sparse, without any message, and constraints added to the copy afterwards are frozen again, so one model ends up with both kinds.

Cause: `copy` rebuilds each constraint as `Constraint(con.mutable().data, ...)` ([`linopy/io.py:1380-1390`](https://github.com/PyPSA/linopy/blob/b9a698bed8ab561a5840d17bf8843c07172eb700/linopy/io.py#L1380-L1390)).

### Reproducible Example

```python
import pandas as pd

import linopy

m = linopy.Model(freeze_constraints=True)
x = m.add_variables(lower=0, coords=[pd.RangeIndex(3, name="i")], name="x")
m.add_constraints(x >= 1, name="c")

c = m.copy()
print(type(m.constraints["c"]).__name__, m.freeze_constraints)
print(type(c.constraints["c"]).__name__, c.freeze_constraints)
```

Output on master (b9a698be):

```
CSRConstraint True
Constraint True
```

### Expected Behavior

A frozen constraint stays a `CSRConstraint` in the copy (copying its CSR store, respecting `deep=` and `include_solution=`), and a dense constraint stays dense. Relevant for #976, which proposes that a copy of a sparse model stays sparse.

### Installed Versions

<details>

linopy 0.9.1.post1.dev37+gb9a698bed (master b9a698be), Python 3.13.11

</details>

problem_statement.body: ### Version 2026.7.1 ### How did you install UXarray? Source ### What happened? When making a fix for #1444 in PR #1667, we noticed there were far more outliers than expected, in an attempt to clean grid files. One example was this file: In a bit less detail it looks like this: We didn't expect this many non-grid dimensions on the grid, and we assume that n2 is likely supposed to be converted to "two" which is a dimension we expect. We would need to resolve this before proceeding, as we don't want to delete it in our planned cleaning process, if it actually needs to be converted to "two" ### What did you expect to happen? To see "two" as a dimension, not "n2" ### Can you provide a MCVE to repoduce the bug? ```python import warnings from pathlib import Path warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") import uxarray as ux MESHFILES = "../../uxarray/test/meshfiles/" # FESOM2 mesh.diag — nz, nz1, n2, N, n4 mesh_diag = ux.open_grid(MESHFILES + "ugrid/fesom/fesom.mesh.diag.nc") mesh_diag # --- separate cell --- GRID_DIMS = set(ux.conventions.ugrid.DIM_NAMES) print(" dims :", dict(mesh_diag._ds.sizes)) print(" non-grid dims :", [d for d in mesh_diag._ds.sizes if d not in GRID_DIMS]) print(" coords :", list(mesh_diag._ds.coords)) ```

problem_statement.title: clear_out_obsolete_test_names never persists its cleanup: counters iterate keys instead of values
problem_statement.body:
`ListAllTestsResult.clear_out_obsolete_test_names` (`src/mutmut/__main__.py`, lines 421–433 on `main`) filters obsolete test names out of `tests_by_mangled_function_name` correctly, but the guard around `save_stats()` can never be true, so the cleaned state is never written back to `mutants/mutmut-stats.json`.

```python
count_before = sum(len(x) for x in mutmut.tests_by_mangled_function_name)   # line 422
...
count_after  = sum(len(x) for x in mutmut.tests_by_mangled_function_name)   # line 430
if count_before != count_after:
    print(f"Removed {count_before - count_after} obsolete test names")
    save_stats()
```

`tests_by_mangled_function_name` is a `defaultdict(set)` (`src/mutmut/__init__.py`, line 15). Iterating it yields **keys**, so `len(x)` measures the length of each mangled function name, not the size of its test set. The dict comprehension in between preserves every key, so both sums are computed over an identical key set and `count_before == count_after` **always** — not intermittently. The branch is dead: the message never prints and `save_stats()` never runs from here.

### Impact

Limited but persistent. The in-memory filtering happens before `tests_for_mutant_names` is used, so runs are unaffected and no verdict is wrong. What lingers is the file on disk: obsolete node IDs stay in `mutmut-stats.json` indefinitely, unless something else happens to call `save_stats()` in the same process (for example `run_stats_collection` when new tests are found). Anyone reading the stats file therefore sees a state no run has ever used.

### Reproduce

1. Run `mutmut run` on a project until stats are cached.
2. Delete or move one test file.
3. Run `mutmut run` again.
4. `mutants/mutmut-stats.json` still contains that file's node IDs under `duration_by_test` and `tests_by_mangled_function_name`, and `Removed N obsolete test names` is never printed.

### Suggested fix

```python
count_before = sum(len(x) for x in mutmut.tests_by_mangled_function_name.values())
count_after  = sum(len(x) for x in mutmut.tests_by_mangled_function_name.values())
```

in both places, which also makes the reported number mean what the message says.

Observed on 3.7.0; the code is unchanged on `main`. Happy to send a PR if that is easier than fixing it directly.
