problem_statement.title: [Bug]: x_average ignores secondary domains, so DFN LLI is nonzero for graded electrodes
problem_statement.body:
### PyBaMM Version

26.5.0 (the same logic is still on `main` at aa8a48b)

### Python Version

3.13.9 (macOS, arm64)

### Describe the bug

Since 26.4.0 (#5448), `pybamm.x_average` pulls a factor out of a product when that factor is constant in x. To decide this, [`_is_independent_of`](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/blob/aa8a48b19af32548e0a9f0d28255f1d5a1d88fd2/packages/pybamm/src/pybamm/expression_tree/averages.py#L12-L25) looks only at each leaf's **primary** domain. A particle variable such as `c_s` has primary domain `"negative particle"` and secondary domain `"negative electrode"`, so it counts as x-constant even though it varies in x. [`_try_separable`](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/blob/aa8a48b19af32548e0a9f0d28255f1d5a1d88fd2/packages/pybamm/src/pybamm/expression_tree/averages.py#L86-L89) then rewrites

```
x_average(eps_s * r_average(c_s))  ->  x_average(eps_s) * x_average(r_average(c_s))
```

That rewrite is only exact when `eps_s` is uniform in x. Up to v26.3.1, `x_average` split sums only and left products alone ([v26.3.1](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/blob/v26.3.1/src/pybamm/expression_tree/averages.py#L228-L233)).

In the DFN, [total_particle_concentration.py L37-L38 and L51](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/blob/aa8a48b19af32548e0a9f0d28255f1d5a1d88fd2/packages/pybamm/src/pybamm/models/submodels/particle/total_particle_concentration.py#L37-L51) uses exactly this expression. So when the active-material volume fraction varies in x:

- `Total lithium in {negative,positive} electrode [mol]`, `Total lithium in particles [mol]` and `LLI [%]` / `Loss of lithium inventory [%]` ([base_lithium_ion_model.py L166-L173](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/blob/aa8a48b19af32548e0a9f0d28255f1d5a1d88fd2/packages/pybamm/src/pybamm/models/full_battery_models/lithium_ion/base_lithium_ion_model.py#L166-L173)) are wrong. LLI moves away from 0 even though nothing consumes lithium.
- `{Negative,Positive} electrode stoichiometry` and `... volume-averaged concentration [mol.m-3]` come out as unweighted x-averages of `c_s_rav`.

The graded-electrodes example notebook has graded the active-material volume fraction since #5791. With its "Low porosity at separator" profile, `LLI [%]` reads 0.29 % at the end of the 3C discharge.

The same rewrite also hits the RHS of `Loss of lithium due to loss of active material in {domain} electrode [mol]` ([loss_active_material.py L192](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/blob/aa8a48b19af32548e0a9f0d28255f1d5a1d88fd2/packages/pybamm/src/pybamm/models/submodels/active_material/loss_active_material.py#L192)). There, `x_average(c_s_rav * deps_s_dt)` becomes `x_average(c_s_rav) * x_average(deps_s_dt)`, which undoes #4858. I checked one case: DFN (OKane2022) with negative-electrode stress-driven LAM at 10x the shipped rate (positive LAM off), 2 cycles. The lithium balance, including this state, was open by 1.1e-7 mol at both `x_n = 20` and `x_n = 40`. It closed to about 1e-11 mol when I recomputed the averages from the solution. With the full OKane2022 degradation options at the shipped LAM rate, the largest gap I saw over 200 cycles was about 1.4e-6 mol (default solver tolerances), so this part is small.

Two cases are not affected: SPM/SPMe, whose particles are already x-averaged, and a DFN whose `eps_s` stays uniform in x.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import numpy as np
import pybamm

print("PyBaMM", pybamm.__version__)

# 1) Expression tree: x_average(eps * r_average(c_s)) is split into a product of
#    x-averages, although c_s depends on x through its secondary domain.
eps = pybamm.Variable("eps", domain="negative electrode")
c_s = pybamm.Variable(
    "c_s",
    domain="negative particle",
    auxiliary_domains={"secondary": "negative electrode"},
)
print("x_average(eps * r_average(c_s)) ->", pybamm.x_average(eps * pybamm.r_average(c_s)))

# 2) Consequence in the DFN: no degradation, negative-electrode active-material
#    volume fraction graded linearly in x (0.60 -> 0.75), one 1C / C/3 cycle.
#    Nothing consumes lithium, so "LLI [%]" should stay at 0.
model = pybamm.lithium_ion.DFN()
param = pybamm.ParameterValues("Chen2020")
L_n = param["Negative electrode thickness [m]"]
param.update(
    {
        "Negative electrode active material volume fraction": (
            lambda x, y=None, z=None: 0.60 + 0.15 * x / L_n
        )
    }
)
experiment = pybamm.Experiment(
    [
        "Discharge at 1C until 2.5 V",
        "Rest for 1 hour",
        "Charge at C/3 until 4.2 V",
        "Rest for 1 hour",
    ]
)
sim = pybamm.Simulation(model, parameter_values=param, experiment=experiment)
sol = sim.solve()

# Reference: integrate eps_s(x) * c_s_rav(x) over the negative-electrode mesh
A = param["Electrode width [m]"] * param["Electrode height [m]"]
dx = sim.mesh["negative electrode"].d_edges
eps_s = sol["Negative electrode active material volume fraction"].entries
c_rav = sol["R-averaged negative particle concentration [mol.m-3]"].entries
n_neg_ref = A * dx @ (eps_s * c_rav)
n_pos = sol["Total lithium in positive electrode [mol]"].entries
n_ref = n_neg_ref + n_pos
lli_ref = (1 - n_ref / n_ref[0]) * 100

n_neg = sol["Total lithium in negative electrode [mol]"].entries
n_part = sol["Total lithium in particles [mol]"].entries
lli = sol["LLI [%]"].entries

print()
print(f"{'':42s}{'reported':>12s}{'reference':>12s}")
print(f"{'max |LLI [%]|':42s}{np.abs(lli).max():12.3e}{np.abs(lli_ref).max():12.3e}")
print(f"{'LLI [%] at end (after 1 h rest)':42s}{lli[-1]:12.3e}{lli_ref[-1]:12.3e}")
print(
    f"{'max |change in particle lithium| [mol]':42s}"
    f"{np.abs(n_part - n_part[0]).max():12.3e}{np.abs(n_ref - n_ref[0]).max():12.3e}"
)
print(
    f"{'max |neg. Li reported - reference| [mol]':42s}"
    f"{np.abs(n_neg - n_neg_ref).max():12.3e}"
)
```

It runs in about 2 s. The "reference" column sums `eps_s * c_s_rav` over the negative-electrode finite-volume cells (`mesh.d_edges`); the positive electrode, whose `eps_s` is uniform, uses the reported value.

### Relevant log output

```shell
PyBaMM 26.5.0
x_average(eps * r_average(c_s)) -> x-average(eps) * x-average(r-average(c_s))

                                              reported   reference
max |LLI [%]|                                2.581e-01   1.319e-11
LLI [%] at end (after 1 h rest)              1.697e-01  -1.319e-11
max |change in particle lithium| [mol]       6.824e-04   3.486e-14
max |neg. Li reported - reference| [mol]     6.824e-04
```

**Expected:** `x_average(eps * r_average(c_s))` stays a single `x-average(eps * r-average(c_s))`, and the reported LLI matches the reference (about 1e-11 %).

**Actual:** the reported LLI peaks at 0.26 % during the cycle and still reads 0.17 % after the final rest, while the lithium actually held in the particles is conserved to 3.5e-14 mol. With a uniform `eps_s = 0.75`, the same script reports LLI of 1.5e-11 %.

### Suggested fix

In `_is_independent_of`, count a leaf as x-dependent if **any** of its domains matches, not just the primary one:

```python
for node in symbol.pre_order():
    if isinstance(node, pybamm.Variable | pybamm.SpatialVariable) and any(
        domain_matches(dom) for doms in node._domains.values() for dom in doms
    ):
        return False
return True
```

I monkey-patched this into 26.5.0 and got these results:

- The repro above gives `x-average(eps * r-average(c_s))` and a reported LLI of 1.3e-11 %.
- The 2-cycle LAM case above closes to 8e-14 mol.
- The 17 tests in the v26.5.0 `tests/unit/test_expression_tree/test_averages.py` still pass. I ran them with `hypothesis` replaced by a fixed input, because it is not installed here.

A regression test could check that `x_average(eps * r_average(c_s))` stays a single `XAverage` when `c_s` has secondary domain `"negative electrode"`.

`ZAverage` and `YZAverage` use the same helper. For example, `z_average(x_average(a) * x_average(b))` is split as well when `a` and `b` have secondary domain `"current collector"`. The change above covers that case too. I have not looked at what that split does to 1+1D results.

### Related (same function)

`_try_separable` also splits a `Division` when only the **numerator** is constant. For example, `x_average(2 / (1 + x_n))` becomes `2 / (1 + x_average(x_n))`. `avg(c / f) = c / avg(f)` holds only when `f` is constant, yet the unit tests assert this rewrite ([L193](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/blob/aa8a48b19af32548e0a9f0d28255f1d5a1d88fd2/packages/pybamm/tests/unit/test_expression_tree/test_averages.py#L193), [L208](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/blob/aa8a48b19af32548e0a9f0d28255f1d5a1d88fd2/packages/pybamm/tests/unit/test_expression_tree/test_averages.py#L208), [L450](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/blob/aa8a48b19af32548e0a9f0d28255f1d5a1d88fd2/packages/pybamm/tests/unit/test_expression_tree/test_averages.py#L450)). Splitting a `Division` only when the denominator is constant would be safe. I have not found a built-in model output where this currently changes the numbers.

problem_statement.title: `end;` statement is unsupported
problem_statement.body:
## Limitation

The [classical instructions](https://openqasm.com/versions/3.1/language/classical.html) chapter defines: "The statement
`end;` immediately terminates the program, no matter what scope it appears in."

`pyqasm` has no handler for `openqasm3.ast.EndStatement` and falls through to the generic
unsupported-statement error.

## Example QASM failure

```qasm
OPENQASM 3.0;
include "stdgates.inc";
qubit[1] q;
h q[0];
end;
```

```
ValidationError: Unsupported statement of type <class 'openqasm3.ast.EndStatement'>
```

Inside a branch, which is the form that carries real meaning:

```qasm
OPENQASM 3.0;
int[8] i = 0;
if (i == 0) { end; }
// ValidationError: Unsupported statement of type <class 'openqasm3.ast.EndStatement'>
```

## Change Requested

1. Accept `end;` wherever a statement is allowed — global scope, loop bodies, `if`/`else`
   blocks, `switch` cases, `box` bodies, and subroutine bodies.
2. At global scope, stop visiting subsequent statements: everything after `end;` is
   unreachable and must not appear in the unrolled output.
3. Preserve `end;` through `dumps()`.
4. Inside a conditional block whose condition depends on a runtime value, `end;` cannot be
   resolved at analysis time. Emit it into the unrolled output as-is rather than attempting to
   truncate the program.

## Implementation Details

- Add an `EndStatement` branch to the statement dispatch in `src/pyqasm/visitor.py`; the
  current fallback that raises is at `visitor.py:3492`.
- The unconditional global-scope case is the simple one: set a flag and stop consuming
  statements at that level.
- Consider whether `QasmModule` should expose that the program contains a terminating `end;` —
  it is the kind of fact the existing `has_measurements()` / `has_barriers()` helpers report,
  and downstream consumers may want it.
- Sanity-check the depth and qubit-count bookkeeping: statements after a global `end;` must
  not contribute, since they are unreachable.
- Tests: `tests/qasm3/test_statements.py` — `end;` at global scope with trailing statements
  that must be dropped, `end;` inside `if`, inside a `for` body, inside a subroutine, and a
  `dumps()` round-trip.

### Describe your environment

OS: debian
Python version: 3.11.2
SDK version: 1.31 & 1.24
API version: 1.31 & 1.24


### What happened?

I expect the following code to show both gauge & counter every 1s in the console (or when scrapped by prometheus client) but it does not. counter is always there. gauge is there when launching the script (very first seconds) then disapears.

```

import random
import time

from prometheus_client import start_http_server

from opentelemetry.exporter.prometheus import PrometheusMetricReader
from opentelemetry.metrics import get_meter_provider, set_meter_provider
from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics import MeterProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics.export import (
    ConsoleMetricExporter,
    PeriodicExportingMetricReader,
)

# Start Prometheus client
start_http_server(port=8000, addr="0.0.0.0")
# Exporter to export metrics to Prometheus
prefix = "MyAppPrefix"
reader = PrometheusMetricReader(prefix)
reader2 = PeriodicExportingMetricReader(ConsoleMetricExporter(), export_interval_millis=1_000)
# Meter is responsible for creating and recording metrics
set_meter_provider(MeterProvider(metric_readers=[reader, reader2]))
meter = get_meter_provider().get_meter("view-name-change", "0.1.2")

my_counter = meter.create_counter("my.counter")
my_gauge = meter.create_gauge("my.gauge")

while 1:
    my_gauge.set(random.randint(1, 10))
    my_counter.add(random.randint(1, 10))
    time.sleep(61)
```


### Steps to Reproduce

run the script above

### Expected Result

gauge to be exported properly

### Actual Result

gauge is not exported properly

_No response_

problem_statement.title: Retry and timeout configuration for REST catalog
problem_statement.body:
### Feature Request / Improvement

**Problem statement**
REST Catalog client uses `requests` library to perform HTTP calls. Currently, if there is an intermittent network/server problem resulting in an error code being returned, `pyiceberg` library would not retry. This is a common problems for out-of-box `requests` usage. Also timeout for the calls is not set.

**Solution outline**
Since retrying/timeout functionalities are very much needed for any HTTP clients, there are classes, available off-the-shelf, which can be used:
* `urllib3.util.retry.Retry` - to define strategy
* `requests.adapters.HTTPAdapter` - to use the strategy

`HTTPAdapter` object can be mounted by request's `session`. 
Timeout could be provided directly to the http calls made by the `session`, but even better `HTTPAdapter` is commonly extended, to include the timeout parameter in all calls.

There would need to be couple of new parameters provided to the catalog config. They could look as below:
```
       type: 'rest'
       uri: "http://localhost:8181"
       connection:
         retry:
           backoff_factor: 0.5
           total: 3
           status_forcelist: [500]
         timeout: 120
```
`retry` key value could be fed directly into the `__init__` of urllibs [Retry](https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/urllib3.util.html#urllib3.util.Retry) class.

problem_statement.title: [BUG] Surface inference uses vertex order instead of mesh connectivity
problem_statement.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Operating system

- [x] Linux
- [ ] Mac
- [ ] Windows

### Operating system version

Linux

### Python version

- [ ] 3.14
- [ ] 3.13
- [x] 3.12
- [ ] 3.11

### nilearn version

0.14.1; also reproduced on main 6e108e6c06a1aadc9ac4170fb588a4e83f8a24a6

### Expected behavior

Relabeling the vertices of an unchanged surface mesh must not change cluster-level inference. Clusters should follow mesh faces.

### Current behavior & error messages

Surface cluster inference groups consecutive array positions. On a 100-vertex mesh where vertices 0, 2, and 4 are connected by faces and all have z=3.1, the function reports 0 at those vertices. Relabeling the same mesh so they are consecutive reports 2/3.

The same topology-preserving control changes 326/20,484 output vertices on the bundled fsaverage5 thickness fixture and 974/20,484 on bundled NeuroVault image 10426 projected to fsaverage5.

Cause: `_cluster_level_inference_surface` calls `scipy.ndimage.label` on a one-dimensional vertex array. That connects neighboring indices, not neighboring mesh vertices. Nilearn's `find_surface_clusters` uses the faces correctly.

Evidence, hashes, full runnable scripts, and tested patch:
https://cheerfulduck.com/research/audits/nilearn-surface-cluster-connectivity

Limits: this demonstrates a software defect and changed numerical result on one public statistical map. It does not establish an affected publication or changed scientific conclusion. No exact prior report was found after bounded issue/PR searches.

### Steps and code to reproduce bug

```python
import numpy as np
from nilearn.glm import cluster_level_inference
from nilearn.surface import InMemoryMesh, SurfaceImage

n = 100
xyz = np.c_[np.arange(n), np.arange(n) % 2, np.zeros(n)]
faces = []
for start in (0, 1):
    v = np.arange(start, n, 2)
    faces.extend([v[i:i+3] for i in range(len(v)-2)])
mesh = InMemoryMesh(xyz.astype(float), np.asarray(faces))
right = InMemoryMesh(xyz[:3].astype(float), np.array([[0, 1, 2]]))
values = np.zeros(n); values[[0, 2, 4]] = 3.1
img = SurfaceImage(mesh={"left": mesh, "right": right}, data={"left": values, "right": np.zeros(3)})
mask = SurfaceImage(mesh=img.mesh, data={"left": np.ones(n, bool), "right": np.zeros(3, bool)})
print(cluster_level_inference(img, mask_img=mask, threshold=3, alpha=.05).data.parts["left"][[0, 2, 4]])
# Current: [0. 0. 0.]; mesh-connectivity result: [0.66666667] * 3
```

+    # Vertical chunking with 'level' key and string representation

problem_statement.title: z3fdb troubles
problem_statement.body:
### machine

Lumi

### catalog

ci

### version

main

### What happened?

There are a couple of issues with using the z3fdb engine.

1) The backend filters unknown kwargs and considers `config_fdb` unknown. As a result, this code 

````
from aqua import Reader
reader = Reader(catalog='ci', model='IFS', exp='test-fdb', source="fdb", engine="z3fdb", config_fdb="/users/jvonhar/config.yaml")
data = reader.retrieve()
````

leads to 

````
2026-09-18 14:27:06 :: BackendIntakeFDB :: WARNING  -> kwarg config_fdb is not in the intake parameters of the source, removing it
````

2) In the latest z3fdb v 5.23.2.27 ECMWF has changed the API of `SimpleStoreBuilder.add_part()` which now accepts a dictionary and not a string for the request (!!)
So z3fdb breaks in newer environments

See https://sites.ecmwf.int/docs/fdb/5.23.5/z3fdb/api.html#z3fdb-simplestorebuilder
